cards.issue_title: All, Public, and Private are exclusive buttons, not checkboxes both on
summary_4_lines: On Explore banks, Bank type is three buttons — All, Public, Private — and only one can be on at a time.
They said Public and Private should both be ticked by default, and All is not a separate filter.
They said the same exclusive-button pattern is wrong for Floating vs Fixed and Term loan vs Overdraft.
They compared it to checkboxes they have seen on Apple and Amazon, where more than one can stay on.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks Filters, Bank type is an exclusive All/Public/Private control; they said Public and Private should both be ticked by default and All is not a separate filter — and they said the same exclusive-button pattern is wrong for Floating/Fixed and Term loan/Overdraft.
cards.on_screen_object: Filters > Bank type exclusive pills All / Public / Private (same exclusive pattern on Rate Floating/Fixed and Facility Term loan/Overdraft)
quotes_sample: Both are ticked by default. All is not a separate filter.
Why do we need a separate button?
related_discussion_one_liners: Apple/Amazon analogy for multi-select checkboxes (not an Apple/Amazon bug on this site); “What is the difference? Why do we need a button?”
Confused by exclusive pills vs ticking several boxes; “I feel the same when I press and hold one button.”
Filter gaps between heading and subheading praised (“these gaps actually work”) — not an issue.

Mobile vs desktop aside while still on the exclusive pills — not a separate named defect; later “keep both of them selected by default” restates the same default-both-on rule (also sits with issue-04).
Empty lender table when Private is exclusive was on screen; they did not call the empty results a defect.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is Bank type / Rate / Facility as exclusive one-at-a-time buttons instead of checkboxes both on, not missing public-vs-private or floating-vs-fixed trade-off copy, not unexplained Overdraft, and not concessions Learn more or missing Back.

cards.issue_title: Concessions Learn more takes you off the filter instead of explaining each option there
summary_4_lines: On Explore banks, Concessions has one small i next to the heading, then Learn more that opens another page.
They said do not take the user to someone else — write the facts on the concessions filter.
Each option (Women applicant, Green home, Insurance) also needs its own i, because they need to know what Insurance concessions are without leaving.
They used the other page only to talk through first name on the papers, the 0.05–0.3 range, and stacking woman + green home.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, Concessions has one heading tooltip plus Learn more that leaves the page; they said do not take the user somewhere else, write the facts on the filter, and give each option (including Insurance) its own i.
cards.on_screen_object: Filters > Concessions heading i-tooltip and Learn more link (div#hlc-help-concessions > a); Women applicant / Green home / Insurance checkboxes with no per-option i
quotes_sample: You shouldn't take this to someone else.
But each of these options also need to have their own eye information.
Because I need to know what insurance concessions are.
related_discussion_one_liners: Opened About Borrower heading i before Concessions — not named as its own defect in this stretch.
On the concessions page they decoded first name on the property: multiple names can be on the papers; she has to be one of them / an individual.
“Nice, bro.” twice while reading the cards — praise of the Guide content, not of taking people there from the filter.
Range talk: 0.05 to 0.3 or 0.2 as total discounts; stacking “woman and greenhouse” (Green home); still wanted local i, not more Guide prose.
Missing Back on the destination is issue-03, not this file.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is Concessions Learn more leaving Explore banks plus only one heading i instead of per-option i on the filter, not the destination page missing Back, and not the exclusive-button or trade-off/overdraft copy issues.

cards.issue_title: Concessions page has no Back after Learn more
summary_4_lines: Learn more from Explore banks opens the concessions Guide page.
That page’s header is Guide plus Explore banks — there is no Back.
They said “No back. Where is the back?” and “This is mobile.”
They had to leave by using the Guide chrome, then return to Explore banks.
cards.pinpoint: After Learn more from Explore banks, the concessions Guide page has no Back; they asked where the back is and said this is mobile.
cards.on_screen_object: Guide header on concessions.html (Guide wordmark, chapter nav, Explore banks CTA) — no Back control
related_discussion_one_liners: “Is this blue?” immediately before “No back.” — likely the Explore banks / Guide chrome color, not a separate named color defect.
“Nice, bro.” while reading concession cards — content praise, not navigation.
They did get back via Guide header / goto explore-banks; that path is what they used, not a Back button.
Off-page Learn more as the reason they were here is issue-02.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is the concessions Guide destination missing a Back control after Learn more, not Learn more taking you off the filter, and not the Explore banks exclusive-button, trade-off, or Overdraft issues.

cards.issue_title: Filters do not tell you why to pick Public vs Private or Floating vs Fixed
summary_4_lines: On Explore banks, Bank type and Rate are just labels. Fixed only says it is about 1–2% higher.
They listed real trade-offs themselves (public process is hard, service, rate about 0.5, processing fee vs private).
Then they asked: tell me what I should select — and keep both selected by default.
They said put those trade-offs here only, including why to pick Floating vs Fixed.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks Filters, Bank type and Rate do not explain the trade-offs, so they asked what they should select; they said tell the public-vs-private and floating-vs-fixed trade-offs here only, and keep both selected by default.
cards.on_screen_object: Filters > Bank type All/Public/Private and Rate Floating/Fixed (Fixed only has “About 1–2% higher”)
quotes_sample: Tell me what should I select?
You tell me the trade-offs here only.
Why I should select each of them? For floating and fixed.
related_discussion_one_liners: Public trade-offs they supplied: application process a little difficult; complete end-to-end service not good; but the rate is 0.5.
Private trade-offs they supplied: service not that good; rates not as good as public; processing fee also not that good.
“And you keep both of them selected by default” overlaps issue-01’s default-both-on rule; kept here as part of “what should I select?”
Fixed’s “About 1–2% higher” is the only on-screen hint; they still asked for floating vs fixed trade-offs.
Empty results when they later left Private+Fixed+Overdraft on were not discussed as this issue.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is missing decision copy on Bank type and Rate so a customer knows why to pick each, not the exclusive-button control (issue-01) and not unexplained Overdraft (issue-05).

cards.issue_title: Overdraft facility is unexplained beyond a higher-rate note
summary_4_lines: On Explore banks, Facility is Term loan or Overdraft. Overdraft only says it is about 0.15–1% higher.
They asked what that facility is (the transcript said “order of facility”).
They then explained a savings-linked overdraft themselves: loan 20 lakh, 5 lakh in savings, interest on 15 lakh, extra cost about 0.25.
They said you should explain it like this — it is very important.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, Overdraft is not explained except “About 0.15–1% higher”; they asked what that facility is, explained savings-linked overdraft themselves, and said the page should explain it like that.
cards.on_screen_object: Filters > Facility exclusive pills Term loan / Overdraft (Overdraft sublabel “About 0.15–1% higher”)
quotes_sample: What is an order of an order of facility?
There is a normal loan which is linked to your savings account.
You should explain it like this. We should learn this. It is very important.
related_discussion_one_liners: Exclusive Term/Overdraft buttons are also part of issue-01’s “same here” uniformity talk; this file is the missing explanation, not the exclusive control.
Worked example: 20 lakh loan, 5 lakh in savings, interest on 15 lakh; take out or keep the 5 lakh.
Cost they stated “more than 0.25 interest” vs on-screen “About 0.15–1% higher” — teaching the idea, not auditing the 0.15–1 band.
People with a lot of cash can keep money there; “I don't have any other option.”
Empty Private+Fixed+Overdraft results in late screenshots were not discussed.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is Overdraft unexplained except a higher-rate note, not the exclusive Facility pills (issue-01) and not missing Public/Private or Floating/Fixed trade-off copy (issue-04).
